📚 Southern Sociological Theory (Global Knowledge Movements in Social Science) | Author: Raewyn Connell | Translator: Hadi Nouri | First Edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publishing | 1405 | The book Southern Sociological Theory offers a framework for radically rethinking the social sciences and their relationship to knowledge, power, and democracy on a global scale—not merely within Western cultural frameworks. The mainstream of social science presents an image of the world as drawn by educated and affluent people in Europe and North America. Theorists from the countries of the Global North dominate the minds, feelings, and imaginations of social scientists and the list of study topics for students around the world. For most of modern history, the majority of the world has been regarded by social science as merely a source of data. Yet the Global South is engaged in producing knowledge and understanding of society. Through vivid narratives about critics and theorists, Raewyn Connell shows how social theory about the world—from Sayyid Jamal al-Din Asadabadi at the dawn of modern social science to Raúl Prebisch in the process of Latin American industrialization, Ali Shariati in revolutionary Iran, Paulin Hountondji in postcolonial Benin, Veena Das and Ashis Nandy in contemporary India, and many others—holds power and significance for understanding our changing world. With clarity and verve, Southern Sociological Theory introduces readers to texts, ideas, and debates that have emerged from the heart of Indigenous peoples in Australia, Africa, Latin America, and South and Southwest Asia. 📚 Faith in the Age of Artificial Intelligence | Author: Don Scott | Translator: Mojtaba Yasbolaghi | First Edition | Naqd-e Farhang Publishing | 1405 | Our world seems to have passed through a looking-glass. Like Alice in the famous story, many religious believers on this new side of the mirror experience things completely upside down. Their attempts to connect with others come to nothing, and others' words seem meaningless to them. They are overcome by dizziness and confusion, and some long with all their heart to return home. Artificial intelligence is the symbol of everything strange and bewildering about an age determined to rewrite reality. By choosing this book, you are likely interested in finding a spiritual and sound way to understand and respond to a culture that grows "stranger and stranger" by the day. To endure and flourish in this world, we need guidance from our spiritual ancestors. We must learn from our postmodern neighbors. And most importantly, we must have a fresh encounter with the Holy Spirit, God and the Giver of life — the One who casts a shadow over things not yet formed to prepare them for the coming of light. One thing is certain: if God has called us to this moment, then we too, like Alice, have been drawn into an adventure. At times it will be frightening, but it will transform us.
